pov: 全章为第三人称限定视角，紧贴 Helena（证明行：L35 Helena felt similarly…；L38 if Helena resembled Cynthia；L155/L161/L197/L263 全是 Helena 的感受与内心）。章内出现的『无引号心声』归属如下：(1) L71『No letter will help the poor mite get a job now.』与 L86『A decision I’ll always regret. How can Georgie ever forgive me?』都不是 Helena 的心声，而是 Mrs Higgins 的念头被 Helena 读心读到——证据：L65『Helena gleaned from Mrs Higgins’ thoughts』、L74『Helena quirked her head at Mrs Higgins’ sentiment』、L83 上文 Higgins 自述『It was my doing that got Lily here in the first place.』与 L86 的 regret 相承。(2) L194、L212、L227、L242、L272 是 Helena 自己的心声（L194 的 me=Helena；L212 紧接 L209 Helena 对天气的观察；L227 Damnation 紧接 Helena 说错话 L218/L230；L242 Hecate help me 紧接 L239 Cynthia 讥讽后 Helena 的反应；L272 紧接 L269 Helena 表态）。(3) L254『We are creatures shaped from the same stardust.』来源不明——L257 明说 Helena『not sure if the thought came from her own mind or the cosmos』，不能武断归给任何人。(4) L131–L149 是 Helena 的旧日记忆闪回，其中引语是当年少女 Helena 与其母 Willow 的对话（出声台词，非心声）。注意：Helena 读不了 Cynthia 的心（L179『why I can’t read her thoughts』），所以全章 Cynthia 的内心只能通过表情动作外推。

events.verbatim: though I won’t be able to match the wages you’ll earn by staying here, Mrs Higgins.’

events.did: 皱起眉头

events.did: 问 Higgins 有没有 Lily 的消息

events.verbatim: ‘I think your gifts are astounding. I would feel safer knowing you are by my side, and knowing when I ask George Lippert my questions, that you would be able to hear his thoughts.

events.did: 说自己也知道被利用是什么滋味、绝不会那样对 Helena；Helena 没有义务陪她去
events.verbatim: But I also know what it is to be used. I won’t do that to you. You are under no obligation to come with me.

events.did: 说可以带上最魁梧的脚夫护身，靠她在 beau monde 的本事辨别真伪，她会没事
events.verbatim: I can take my burliest footmen along for protection and use my skills as a fearsome lady of the beau monde to determine truths from lies. I shall be fine.’

events.did: 心想：没有自己在旁边护着，Cynthia 绝不会有事
events.verbatim: She bloody well won’t be fine without me there to keep her safe.

events.did: 新的恐惧绽开：不是怕在 Cynthia 里迷失自己，而是怕彻底失去她；意识到这个勇敢的女人完全不知自己在凶手与疯子中间有多脆弱
events.verbatim: A new fear blossomed in Helena. Not that she might lose herself in Cynthia, but that she might lose Cynthia altogether. The courageous woman had no idea how vulnerable she was amongst murderers and madmen.

events.did: 说 Cynthia 不能只身去 Cheapside 指控 Lippert 谋杀亲夫，那不像指责某位 debutante 抄了她的礼服那样容易
events.verbatim: ‘You can’t go to Cheapside alone and accuse Lippert of murdering your husband as easily as you might claim some debutante copied your gown.

events.did: 说你哥哥会大发雷霆，Uncle Lachlan 会因她不上报计划而把她倒吊起来
events.verbatim: Your brother would have a fit, and Uncle Lachlan will string me up by my toes for not telling him of your plans.’

events.did: 反诘：你不陪我去，又不许我独自去？讽刺 Helena 这么聪明却尽说胡话
events.verbatim: ‘You won’t go with me, but I can’t go alone? For an intelligent woman, you certainly spew your share of nonsense.

events.did: 宣称自己是寡妇、除自己外无人能支配她的选择；打赌 Helena 也独自做各种事而无人非议，凭什么她就不行
events.verbatim: I am a widow with no one to control my choices but me. I’d wager you do all manner of things alone without a single soul speaking ill of you. Why should I be any different?’

events.did: 站起来，在过软的 Rococo 椅与 Helena 所坐 chaise 之间来回急踱
events.verbatim: Cynthia stood and paced in a tight line from the overstuffed Rococo chair to the chaise where Helena sat and back again.

events.did: 说厌倦了自己一举一动都被人规定：你不想被利用，我不想被支配，这不难理解
events.verbatim: ‘I am tired of my every action being dictated by others. You have no wish to be used, and I have no wish to be controlled. Surely that is not so difficult to understand.’

events.did: 起身挡在 Cynthia 踱步的路线前，逼她要么停步要么撞上自己
events.verbatim: Helena rose, stepping in front of Cynthia’s path and forcing her to stop walking or crash into her.

events.did: 说『No one is controlling you.』
events.verbatim: ‘No one is controlling you.’

events.did: 脸涨红，质问：Hubert 死了不到一个月，我的哥哥、你的叔叔、如今连你都在规定我能去哪能做什么
events.verbatim: ‘Really?’ Cynthia’s face flushed. ‘Not a month since Hubert died, and already my brother, your uncle, and now you are dictating where I can go and what I can do.’

events.did: 抬手止住 Helena 的反驳，说她知道对方好意，但自己不是事事要被代做决定的孩子
events.verbatim: She put her hand up, staying Helena’s counterargument. ‘I know you mean well. But I am not some child whose every choice must be made for her.’

events.did: 窗外天空变暗、起风，猛烈抽打着 hydrangea 花
events.verbatim: The sky outside darkened as a wind picked up, thrashing the hydrangea blooms most violently.

events.did: 控诉社会要求贵族女性做温柔明亮的花朵：只添色彩香气，无观点、无追求、除装饰价值外无目的；她努力活成这愚蠢典范，因为从小被教导守规则、不质疑自己的位置
events.verbatim: ‘Society believes women of the peerage should behave as gentle, bright blossoms. We should bring colour and fragrance into a room but have no opinions, no personal drive, no purpose beyond decorative value. I have worked hard to exemplify this ideal, stupid as it is, because I was raised to follow the rules and never question my place.’

events.did: 一道闪电划破几分钟前还是温暖夏日的、正在变暗的天空；Helena 望向窗外并挑起眉毛
events.verbatim: A crack of lightning in what was moments ago a warm summer day lit the now darkening skies with white-hot electricity. Helena glanced out the window and raised a brow.

events.did: 想起见过这种天气：Aunt Rowan 特别恼怒时她与大地（earth）的连接会以不可预知的方式显形；眼下感觉一模一样
events.verbatim: She’d seen weather like this. When Aunt Rowan was particularly vexed, there was no telling how her connection to the earth would manifest. This felt the same.

events.did: 得出结论：Cynthia 是 earthwitch，就像 Aunt Rowan 一样
events.verbatim: She’s an earthwitch, just like Aunt Rowan.

events.did: 把目光转回 Cynthia 身上，一种刺麻感从头顶漫开、像网一样罩住皮肤
events.verbatim: She returned her gaze to Cynthia, and a prickling sensation began at the top of her head, covering her skin like a web.

events.did: 出声警告『Cynthia, you must remain calm.』；心里承认自己除了童年经历外没有应对新女巫力量觉醒的经验
events.verbatim: ‘Cynthia, you must remain calm.’ Helena had no practice with new witches coming into their power, except for her own experiences as a child.

events.did: 当年 Aunt Rowan 全程引导 Helena、把失控显形的灾难压到最小；而 Cynthia 没有别人，只有 Helena
events.verbatim: But Aunt Rowan had been there to guide her through every step. Whatever rogue manifestations occurred, Aunt Rowan kept the disasters to a minimum. Cynthia had no one. Except Helena.

events.did: Rowan 曾警告 Helena 小心行事：用来封住 Cynthia 魔法的咒似乎正在松动
events.verbatim: Aunt Rowan had warned Helena to tread carefully. Whatever spell had been used to contain Cynthia’s magic seemed to be slipping.

events.did: 交代规则：女巫的魔力七岁显形，此后每七年增强一轮；Cynthia 即将年满二十八
events.verbatim: A witch’s power manifested at seven, then grew more potent every seven years. Cynthia was approaching her twenty-eighth year.

events.did: 担心 Cynthia 的魔法像被堵了太久的奔流，一步走错堤坝就会溃决、释放出强大而具破坏力的力量
events.verbatim: Helena worried her magic was like a rushing river that had been dammed for too long. One wrong move and that dam could break, unleashing a powerful and destructive force.

events.did: 双手叉腰反问『我必须冷静？』，榛色双眼不祥地发光
events.verbatim: ‘I must stay calm?’ Cynthia put her hands on her hips, her hazel eyes glowing ominously.

events.did: 心里暗叫『Damnation.』（糟糕）
events.verbatim: Damnation.

events.did: Cynthia 刚说受够了被人指挥，Helena 却像个十足的傻瓜更进一步，说了愤怒中的女人最不想听的那句话
events.verbatim: Cynthia had just told Helena she was sick of being told what to do, and Helena, like a complete simpleton, had gone a step further by saying the one thing no woman wanted to hear when they were courting fury.

events.did: 双眼几乎因怒火发光，一字一顿吼出『Do. Not. Tell. Me. To. Remain. Calm!』；雷声震得窗玻璃发抖
events.verbatim: Cynthia’s eyes fairly glowed with rage. ‘Do. Not. Tell. Me. To. Remain. Calm!’ Thunder shook the windowpanes.

events.did: 立刻换策略，点头说『你说得对，当然，你想有什么感受就有什么感受』
events.verbatim: Switching tacks, Helena nodded her head. ‘You’re right. Of course. You can feel however you want to feel.’

events.did: 讥讽：『是吗？你真是宽宏大量，居然允许我感受我的感受』
events.verbatim: ‘Can I? How magnanimous of you. To allow me to feel my feelings.’

events.did: 向 Hecate 求助，意识到自己正在把事情越弄越糟
events.verbatim: Hecate help me, I’m making things worse.

events.did: 辩解自己只是想说她们应该谨慎行事
events.verbatim: ‘I only meant that we should proceed with caution.’

events.did: 抓住『We?』这个词反问
events.verbatim: ‘We?’

events.did: 灵巧地从沙发上跳下来，绕到 Cynthia 身边，用头蹭她的腿
events.verbatim: Hamlet hopped nimbly from the couch and wound his way to Cynthia, bumping his head against her leg.

events.did: 心不在焉地低头看狐狸，说『I’m fine』，优雅的手指埋进他双耳之间的铜色皮毛
events.verbatim: Cynthia looked down distractedly at the fox. ‘I’m fine.’ Her elegant fingers disappeared in the copper fur between his ears.

events.did: 认出这是自己对自己的 familiar 做过一百万次的动作；看着 Cynthia 像她一贯那样向 Hamlet 寻求安慰，令她内心深处某物挪动了
events.verbatim: It was a gesture Helena had made a million times with her familiar, but watching Cynthia seeking comfort from Hamlet as Helena always had, shifted something at her centre.

events.did: 念头浮现：『We are creatures shaped from the same stardust.』
events.verbatim: We are creatures shaped from the same stardust.

events.did: 眨眼，不确定这个念头是来自她自己的 mind 还是 cosmos
events.verbatim: She blinked, not sure if the thought came from her own mind or the cosmos.

events.who: Cynthia（原文无 tag，按上下文推断）
events.did: 问：『你是说你要和我一起去？』
events.verbatim: ‘Are you saying you’ll come with me?’

events.did: 意识到自己仍可以退缩，但她每一丁点都想加入 Cynthia 的这场冒险
events.verbatim: Helena could still back away. But every tiny piece of her wanted to join Cynthia on this adventure.

events.did: 在心里补上一句：每一场冒险（都愿意加入）
events.verbatim: On every adventure.

events.did: 答应『Yes, we』，承认自己先前犯蠢；说想帮 Cynthia 找到谋杀她丈夫的混蛋、让她开始新生活，不想她独自面对
events.verbatim: ‘Yes, we. I was being stupid before. I want to help you, Cynthia. I want to find the bastard who murdered your husband so you can start your life anew. And I don’t want you to do this alone.’

events.did: 暗自断定：当 Cynthia 的力量破封而出时，她将需要 Helena 能给的全部帮助
events.verbatim: I’m also quite certain when your power breaks free, you’re going to need all the help I can give.

events.did: 想到陪伴 Cynthia 学习调用魔法、看她步入自己的力量，搅动了她平静的灵魂；女巫连接元素是原始而发自肺腑的事
events.verbatim: The idea of supporting Cynthia as she learned to access her magic, watching her step into her abilities, stirred Helena’s calm soul. It was a raw and visceral thing for a witch to connect to her element.

events.did: 想到别人来担任这个亲密角色就充满 violent jealousy（剧烈的嫉妒）
events.verbatim: Imagining anyone else stepping into such an intimate role filled Helena with violent jealousy.

events.did: 问『你愿意让我帮你吗？』，屏住呼吸，觉得自己的世界悬在 Cynthia 答复的边缘——因为她问的不只是这场调查
events.verbatim: ‘Will you let me help you?’ Helena held her breath, feeling like her world rested on the precipice of Cynthia’s answer. Because she wasn’t just asking about this investigation.

events.did: 呼气，笑容绽开，同时太阳试探性地从暴风云后露出；她说当然愿意让 Helena 帮忙，她从来就不想独自做这件事
events.verbatim: Cynthia exhaled, a smile breaking over her as the sun tentatively peeked through the storm clouds. ‘Of course I will let you help me. I never wanted to do this alone.’

events.who: 说话人未标注（原文无 tag）
events.did: 说『Then we shall do it together.』；最后一个词在 Helena 体内回响如浪拍岩石，她心中一块碎裂的东西咔哒归位
events.verbatim: ‘Then we shall do it together.’ The last word resonated through Helena like the crash of waves over rocks. A fractured piece of her heart clicked into place.

events.did: 叫了一声（yipped），金色的眼睛敏锐得不可思议
events.verbatim: Hamlet yipped, his golden eyes uncannily perceptive.

events.did: 把那种感觉耸开、专注于眼前任务；告诉自己没空担心爱上一个女巫，因为她们要去 confronting 一个可能的凶手
events.verbatim: Helena shrugged away the feeling, instead focusing on the task at hand. She didn’t have time to worry about falling in love with a witch when they were confronting a potential killer.

traps_noted.trap: L35『When the spell was finally broken, she described it…』的 she 指 Aunt Rowan，不是 Helena；且被下过咒的是 Rowan，Helena 从未被下咒。误判后果：把『曾被 hexed、像从催眠中醒来』的经历安到 Helena 头上，人物史实写反。
L38『Cynthia’s mouth was bruised from her kisses』——bruised 的原因是亲吻（her kisses 指 Helena 对她的吻），不是被打伤。误判后果：把这章开场读成家暴/冲突痕迹，或以为 Cynthia 吻伤了别人，性质完全写错。
L41 整理头发方向易反：是 Cynthia 先自己重挽 chignon，再走到 settee 后方替 Helena 把头发别好；此前 Helena 在自己徒劳地整理。误判后果：把『谁帮谁梳妆』的方向调转，两人关系的主动/被动错位。
L44『She chose a new chair opposite Helena』的 She 是 Cynthia——她帮 Helena 弄好头发后没有坐回原处，而是换了一把正对 Helena 的新椅子。误判后果：写成 Helena 换椅子，或漏掉『Cynthia 从 Helena 身后回到对面』这一空间变化（后续 L125 她再次起身绕桌坐到 Helena 旁边）。
L50『Come in.』和 wink 都是 Cynthia 发出的；随后的 thrill/arousal 是 Helena 的感受。误判后果：把台词和眨眼安到 Helena 头上，或把身体反应安到 Cynthia 头上。
L62『she got the chop』是英式口语『被解雇』，不是被杀。误判后果：把 Lily 写成被害人，与后文 Higgins 盼她『quite happy there with her family』（L92）直接矛盾，且把悬疑线彻底带偏。

L71『No letter will help the poor mite get a job now.』与 L86『A decision I’ll always regret. How can Georgie ever forgive me?』都是 Mrs Higgins 的心声（被 Helena 读心读到），不是 Helena 的内心话，也不是说出来的台词。归属证据：L65『Helena gleaned from Mrs Higgins’ thoughts』、L74『Helena quirked her head at Mrs Higgins’ sentiment』。误判后果：把管家的隐秘念头当成 Helena 的判断，等于凭空给 Helena 加上她并不掌握的上帝视角信息。
L80 问句『Lily’s father is George Lippert?』无说话人 tag，同句里 Helena『body tightened』、Cynthia『sat straighter』，两人都可能被读成说话人（原文未裁决，见 U2）。误判后果：精读时武断指定说话人，把 Helena/Cynthia 谁先掌握 Lippert 线索这一关键信息归属搞错。

L107『what you heard from Sinclair』——分工易错：是 Cynthia 当面问 Sinclair 是否杀了她丈夫（L110 When you asked him），而 Helena 是读到 Sinclair 心里想到 Lippert 的名字（L110 he clearly thought）。误判后果：把『审问者』与『读心者』角色互换，或以为 Sinclair 亲口说出了 Lippert 的名字（他是 thought，不是说出口）。
L122『the corresponding thrill fizzing through her veins』的 her 按语境是 Helena（对应她 L50 的 thrill），不是 Cynthia。误判后果：写成 Cynthia 的生理反应，而 Helena 读不到 Cynthia（L179），会造成视角穿帮。
L128–L151 整段是 Helena 的旧记忆闪回，不是当下剧情；其中 L134『she refused to cry out』的 she 是被抓疼的 Helena，而 L140 打人的是 Willow（Her mother had never hit her before 证明母亲=Willow、被打=Helena）。误判后果：把闪回当现在时事件写进情节梳理，或把耳光的施/受双方颠倒。
L152『Cynthia’s warm hand on her face』的 her face 是 Helena 的脸（把她从回忆拉回的是 Cynthia 的手）。误判后果：写成 Cynthia 摸自己的脸，动作归属调转。

L155『Helena leaned away from the comfort』——Helena 躲开的是 Cynthia 的抚慰；L158 Cynthia 因此误以为 Helena 当初『要陪她查案』的承诺不是认真的（You weren’t serious. Of course.）。误判后果：把 L158 读成 Cynthia 主动收回邀请，实际是误会链：Helena 说怕被利用→Cynthia 自认被拒→强笑掩痛。

L164『She was nothing like the man Willow chose. Nothing like her mother.』两个 She 都指 Cynthia——她既不像 Willow 选中的那个男人，也不像 Willow 本人。误判后果：把第二个 Nothing like her mother 读成 Helena 自评『我不像我妈』，把这段对 Cynthia 的极高评价错安到 Helena 的自我安慰上。
L173『she had created this mess』的 she 是 Helena（mess 指刚才的误会），不是 Cynthia。误判后果：把道歉责任方写反——紧接着 L188 Helena 说该请求原谅的是自己。
L194『She bloody well won’t be fine without me there to keep her safe.』是 Helena 的心声：She=Cynthia、me=Helena。误判后果：读成 Cynthia 的自语或第三人称评论，把『保护者是谁』颠倒；注意 Helena 读不到 Cynthia 的心声（L179），所以这句只可能出自 Helena。
亲属关系方向：L200 Helena 对 Cynthia 说『Your brother would have a fit』，L209 Cynthia 说『my brother, your uncle』——Lachlan 是 Cynthia 的兄弟、Helena 的叔叔。误判后果：把 Lachlan 写成 Helena 的兄弟或 Cynthia 的叔叔，人物关系表全错。
L209 起的暴风、L233 震窗的雷声、L281 放晴的阳光都不是天气巧合，而是 Cynthia（earthwitch）情绪的外化——L209 Helena 明说 This felt the same（像 Rowan 发怒时的显形），L212 确认 She’s an earthwitch。误判后果：把风暴写成背景气氛，漏掉本章最大信息点之一（Cynthia 的魔力属性与被封印的魔法正在失控）。
L218『Cynthia, you must remain calm.』是 Helena 说的，而且恰是 L230 点明的『愤怒中的女人最不想听的那句话』——Helena 自己也承认像 complete simpleton。误判后果：把这句警告读成专业而正确的处置，忽略它直接引爆 L233 的怒吼与雷声。
L227『Damnation.』是 Helena 的心声（紧接 L224 Cynthia 眼神不祥、L230 Helena 自省），不是 Cynthia 骂出声。误判后果：给 Cynthia 加一句她没说过的台词。
Hamlet 是狐狸（fox，L251），是 Helena 的 familiar，性别为雄性（his/wound his way/copper fur/golden eyes）。误判后果：写成猫、狗或 Cynthia 的宠物，把 L251『Cynthia 像 Helena 一贯那样向 Hamlet 寻求安慰』这一触动 Helena 的关键细节读丢。
L254『We are creatures shaped from the same stardust.』来源不明，L257 原文自己说 Helena 不确定来自自己的 mind 还是 cosmos。误判后果：武断归给 Helena、Hamlet 或 Cynthia 任何一方，替原文下了它明确拒绝下的结论。
L260『Are you saying you’ll come with me?』无 tag，但按上下文是 Cynthia 在问 Helena（承接 L248 Cynthia 的『We?』和 L245 Helena 说的 we should proceed with caution）。误判后果：读成 Helena 在问，邀约方向反转，L269 Helena 的『Yes, we』就接不上了。
L284 说话人无 tag（见 U7）：『Then we shall do it together.』后接 resonated through Helena，既可读成 Cynthia 说给 Helena 听，也可读成 Helena 自己的话在她体内回响。误判后果：引语归属写死后与后续章的引用对不上。
L290『falling in love with a witch』——Helena 在章末仍把这句话当作自我否认（shrugged away the feeling），她此前 L179 也坚称 That is not love；不能据此写『Helena 已承认爱上 Cynthia』。误判后果：把叙述层的暗示当成人物已完成的心理转变，抢跑了原文留白。

L209 时序陷阱：闪电那句先说『A crack of lightning』再补『in what was moments ago a warm summer day』——温暖夏日在前、天色转暗与闪电在后，都发生在 Cynthia 怒火升级的过程里；雷震窗玻璃（L233）又在怒吼『Do. Not. Tell. Me. To. Remain. Calm!』之后同句发生。误判后果：把天气变化排到争吵之前，丢掉『情绪→天象』的因果同步。
L1–L22 的『Chapter 16』『16』是书籍提取件的章节标题行，不是正文；本章正文从 L35 才开始，且无场景标题。误判后果：把章号当正文内容分析，或误以为 L1–L34 之间漏了内容。
L59『the wages you’ll earn by staying here』的比较方向易错：Cynthia 说自己开不出 Higgins 留在原处能挣到的工钱（所以带不走她）——是 Cynthia 出不起更高的价，不是 Higgins 嫌钱少要走。误判后果：把主仆对话写成 Higgins 主动求去。
